title: Indonesia’s Franky Widjaja resigns as palm oil giant’s commissioner
text:
Indonesia’s Franky Widjaja resigns as palm oil giant’s commissioner Thursday 19 Nov 2026 BURSA SGX Home 
 Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google (Nov 18): Indonesian tycoon Franky Oesman Widjaja has resigned as president commissioner of one of the nation’s largest palm oil producers, ending a 23-year run in the post and marking his second board departure from a Sinar Mas group company in about two months.
 Franky, 68, left PT Sinar Mas Agro Resources and Technology and was replaced by David Fernando Audy following a shareholders’ meeting in Jakarta on Tuesday, the company said in a stock exchange filing. 
 Franky had held the post since 2003 and was reappointed in June 2025 to a five-year term. He remains chairman and chief executive of Golden Agri-Resources Ltd, the Singapore-listed parent company of Sinar Mas Agro.
 In an emailed comment, Sinar Mas Agro described the change as “part of regular review of leadership and governance process”, without elaborating.
 The move follows Franky’s September resignation as president commissioner of PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa, a Sinar Mas group mining and energy company, where David also replaced him. 
 The resignations come against a backdrop of increased scrutiny of Sinar Mas group companies by authorities on several fronts.
 In October, an Indonesian regulator fined the controlling shareholder of Dian Swastatika 1.5 trillion rupiah (US$82.2 million or RM340 million) for misconduct related to alleged stock-market manipulation. The same month, Franky was among eight business leaders summoned by Singaporean authorities over their companies’ alleged links to land fires in Indonesia that caused regional haze that also affected neighbouring Singapore, Malaysia and the Philippines.
